title: Phase-aligned windowed communication scheduler and kernel hedging for multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Current multi-GPU prefill/decode paths suffer from tail latency spikes and suboptimal NCCL utilization when tensor and pipeline parallel stages drift out of phase. We observe intermittent stalls when large prefill batches align poorly with downstream decode windows, and kernel selection sometimes chooses heavy fused kernels that increase overlap contention under specific sequence length distributions.

Goal:
Design and implement a phase-aligned scheduling layer that: (1) maintains a sliding 'comm window' per-device to concentrate NCCL collectives into predictable overlap-friendly intervals, (2) applies lightweight kernel hedging rules that prefer lower-latency kernels when comm windows are congested, and (3) exposes runtime knobs for burst-reservation and soft backpressure to preserve tail SLOs.

Proposed approach:
- Add a WindowedCommCoordinator module in the runtime scheduler that tracks per-stage token cadence and opens a comm window of configurable width (ms) and hysteresis. When a window is open, NCCL/all-reduce operations are allowed to aggregate; outside the window, we route smaller collectives or fall back to ring-tree alternatives.
- Implement PhaseEstimator to infer drift between adjacent pipeline/tensor stages using light-weight timestamps on prefill/first-decode tokens. Use EWMA to smooth estimates and trigger window realignment only when drift exceeds threshold.
- Kernel hedging: introduce a selection policy that considers current comm window occupancy and expected waiting time. If the coordinator predicts a comm stall, pick kernels with slightly higher FLOP-efficiency but lower memory movement (favoring streaming attention kernels) to reduce cross-device contention.
- Backpressure and soft-priority: allow foreground low-latency traffic (e.g., low-length queries with critical SLO) to preempt batching within limits, by offering a reserved fast-path that uses single-GPU-prefill or smaller microbatches.

Success criteria / acceptance tests:
- Reduce 99th-percentile latency for mixed prefill/decode workload by at least 20% in our heterogeneous 8xA100 testbed vs baseline scheduler.
- NCCL utilization must be >= 85% during sustained batched prefill phases while decode-phase stalls reduce by >= 30%.
- No regression in median latency or throughput for standard benchmark (long-context generation).

Implementation tasks:
- [ ] Design data model for comm windows and phase state; add metrics and tracing hooks (runtime tracing, per-request tags).
- [ ] PhaseEstimator prototype in Python harness; validate on trace replay dataset.
- [ ] Integrate WindowedCommCoordinator into C++ scheduler, add kernel policy switchpoints.
- [ ] Add kernel profiling counters used for hedging decisions.
- [ ] End-to-end benchmark harness and A/B test runner to compare baseline vs windowed scheduler under controlled drift scenarios.
- [ ] Docs: runtime config knobs, dashboard panels for comm windows and phase drift, upgrade notes for Dedicated customers.

Artifacts/links:
- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Phase+Alignment+Design (draft)
- Trace corpus: gs://redwood-runtime-traces/prefill-decode/2025-01
- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021 (WIP)

Risks and trade-offs:
- Over-aggressive windowing could increase short-term queuing and hurt median latency; mitigated by hysteresis and per-customer soft limits.
- Kernel hedging requires accurate microbenchmarks; long tail of hardware-specific behavior may mean per-hardware tuning required.
- Exposing too many knobs harms self-serve experience; will provide sane defaults and an autosuggest tune from Redwood Optimize in later iteration.

comments: 2025-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Spun up trace replays from the 8xA100 cluster; initial traces show 60-200ms microdrift between stages depending on inter-op queuing. Added PhaseEstimator spike detector to flag samples.

2025-02-16 - Liam Chen: Prototype PhaseEstimator implemented in Python. Replay shows window width of 20ms with 10ms hysteresis reduces cross-stage misalignment by ~40% on synthetic traces. Will port algorithm to C++ and add low-overhead timestamping.

2025-02-20 - SRE Review (N. Patel): Concerned about additional timers increasing wakeups. Recommendation: batch timestamp updates and piggyback on existing request lifecycle hooks. Marked SLO impact as medium.

2025-02-24 - Design feedback (R. Alvarez): Prefer using a percentile-based threshold for drift triggers (e.g., 90th perc) rather than fixed ms to avoid sensitivity to noisy traces. Also requested dashboard mockups for comm window occupancy.

2025-02-28 - Liam Chen: Integrated coordinator skeleton into scheduler; running internal canary. Early numbers: 99p down 8% on one workload; need kernel hedging to unlock further gains. Planning kernel microbench run this week.
